binders: A type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A sequence X of real-valued functions X_i: Ω→ℝ indexed by natural numbers.
hypotheses: The expectation of S_N(ω)=∑_{i=0}^{N-1}X_i(ω) equals Nm.
The variance of S_N equals Nσ².
mathematical_definitions: The right-hand normalized centered sum is (σ√N)⁻¹∑_{i=0}^{N-1}(X_i-m).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a positive number N of real-valued functions and a positive scale σ, if their finite sum has mean Nm and variance Nσ², then standardizing the sum by subtracting its expectation and dividing by its standard deviation gives exactly the same function as summing the individually m-centered terms and multiplying by 1/(σ√N).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement assumes the aggregate mean and variance formulas instead of deriving them from independence, identical distribution, individual means, or individual variances.

No measurability, integrability, probability-measure, or finiteness hypotheses are imposed explicitly; expectation and variance are total definitions, so the assumed equalities may not represent ordinary probabilistic moments without additional analytic hypotheses.
The hypotheses 0<N and 0<σ exclude the zero-size and zero-scale cases and ensure the intended denominators are positive.
The conclusion is an equality of functions everywhere, not merely almost everywhere.
The index set is 0 through N-1.
The result is an algebraic normalization identity and does not assert convergence or a central limit theorem.
ambiguities: It is not specified whether μ is intended to be a probability measure.
The functions X_i are not explicitly identified as random variables because measurability is absent.
The parameters m and σ are characterized only through aggregate moment equalities; they are not explicitly declared to be the common mean and standard deviation of the individual X_i.
The choice of zero-based indexing may require reindexing when compared with a convention using indices 1 through N.
